mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the past month signals an accommodative monetary policy stance that reduces the cost of capital for corporations, leading to higher equity valuations and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of the months when FEDFUNDS declines, or the Rank IC over the last 3 years is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate exceeds 6.0% for two consecutive months, it signals a weakening labor market that may prompt central bank intervention, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate policy support.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of the instances when UNRATE > 6.0%, or the Rank IC over the last 3 years is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and a rise in consumer credit (RSAFS) indicates a weakening demand environment that triggers a flight to quality in equities, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of the instances when both HOUST declines and RSAFS rises, or the Rank IC over the last 3 years is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: During a period of rising industrial production (INDPRO > 105) and falling unemployment (UNRATE < 5.0%), the economy is in a late-cycle expansion phase where corporate earnings growth is slowing, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of the instances when INDPRO > 105 and UNRATE < 5.0%, or the Rank IC over the last 3 years is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: A rising consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) above 2.5% annually signals persistent inflation that may lead to aggressive monetary tightening, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The 5-day forward returns are negative in less than 45% of the months when CPIAUCSL rises above 2.5%, or the Rank IC over the last 3 years is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in retail sales (RSAFS) above its 3-month moving average indicates strong consumer spending that supports corporate revenues, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of the months when RSAFS is above its 3-month moving average, or the Rank IC over the last 3 years is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly change in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) falls below 50.0 (representing 50,000 persons), it signals a slowing labor market that may lead to economic uncertainty, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns are negative in less than 45% of the instances when PAYEMS < 50.0, or the Rank IC over the last 3 years is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) falls below 105.0, it signals a contraction in manufacturing activity that may lead to reduced corporate profits, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The 5-day forward returns are negative in less than 45% of the instances when INDPRO < 105.0, or the Rank IC over the last 3 years is below 0.02.
